verses.zh: 我 是 因 耶 和 華 忿 怒 的 杖 ， 遭 遇 困 苦 的 人 。
verses.en: א (Alef)[NOTE:1] I am the man[NOTE:2] who has experienced[NOTE:3] afflictionfrom the rod[NOTE:4] of the Lord’s wrath.
notes: The nature of the acrostic changes here. Each of the three lines in each verse, not just the first, begins with the corresponding letter of the alphabet.

The noun גֶּבֶר (gever, “man”) refers to a strong man, distinguished from women, children, and other non-combatants whom he is to defend. According to W. F. Lanahan the speaking voice in this chapter is that of a defeated soldier (“The Speaking Voice in the Book of Lamentations” JBL 93 [1974]: 41-49.) F. W. Dobbs-Allsopp (Lamentations [IBC], 108) argues that is the voice of an “everyman,” although “one might not unreasonably suppose that some archetypal communal figure like the king does in fact stand in the distant background.”

The verb רָאָה (raʾah, “to see”) has a broad range of meanings, including (1) “to see” as to learn from experience and (2) “to see” as to experience (e.g., Gen 20:10; Ps 89:49; Eccl 5:17; Jer 5:12; 14:13; 20:18; 42:14; Zeph 3:15). Here it means that the speaker has experienced these things. The same Hebrew verb occurs in 2:20, where the Lord is asked to “see” (translated “Consider!”), although it is difficult to maintain this connection in an English translation.

The noun שֵׁבֶט (shevet, “rod”) refers to the weapon used for smiting an enemy (Exod 21:20; 2 Sam 23:21; 1 Chr 11:3; Isa 10:15; Mic 4:14 HT [5:1 ET]) and to the instrument of child-discipline (Prov 10:13; 22:15; 29:15). It is used figuratively to describe discipline of the individual (Job 9:34; 21:9; 37:13; 2 Sam 7:14; Ps 89:33) and the nation (Isa 10:5, 24; 14:29; 30:31).

The same Hebrew verb occurs in 2:20, where the Lord is asked to “see” (translated “Consider!”), although it is difficult to maintain this connection in an English translation.

verses.zh: 我 求 告 你 的 日 子 ， 你 臨 近 我 ， 說 ： 不 要 懼 怕 ！
verses.en: You came near[NOTE:1] on the day I called to you;you said,[NOTE:2] “Do not fear!”
notes: The nature of the acrostic changes here. Each of the three lines in each verse, not just the first, begins with the corresponding letter of the alphabet.

The noun גֶּבֶר (gever, “man”) refers to a strong man, distinguished from women, children, and other non-combatants whom he is to defend. According to W. F. Lanahan the speaking voice in this chapter is that of a defeated soldier (“The Speaking Voice in the Book of Lamentations” JBL 93 [1974]: 41-49.) F. W. Dobbs-Allsopp (Lamentations [IBC], 108) argues that is the voice of an “everyman,” although “one might not unreasonably suppose that some archetypal communal figure like the king does in fact stand in the distant background.”

verses.zh: 主 啊 ， 你 伸 明 了 我 的 冤 ； 你 救 贖 了 我 的 命 。

verses.zh: 耶 和 華 啊 ， 你 見 了 我 受 的 委 屈 ； 求 你 為 我 伸 冤 。
verses.en: You have seen the wrong done to me, O Lord;pronounce judgment on my behalf![NOTE:1]
notes: The nature of the acrostic changes here. Each of the three lines in each verse, not just the first, begins with the corresponding letter of the alphabet.

verses.zh: 他 們 仇 恨 我 ， 謀 害 我 ， 你 都 看 見 了 。
verses.en: You have seen all their vengeance,all their plots against me.[NOTE:1]
notes: The nature of the acrostic changes here. Each of the three lines in each verse, not just the first, begins with the corresponding letter of the alphabet.

verses.zh: 耶 和 華 啊 ， 你 聽 見 他 們 辱 罵 我 的 話 ， 知 道 他 們 向 我 所 設 的 計 ，
verses.en: ש (Sin/Shin)You have heard[NOTE:1] their taunts, O Lord,all their plots against me.
notes: The nature of the acrostic changes here. Each of the three lines in each verse, not just the first, begins with the corresponding letter of the alphabet.

verses.zh: 並 那 些 起 來 攻 擊 我 的 人 口 中 所 說 的 話 ， 以 及 終 日 向 我 所 設 的 計 謀 。
verses.en: My assailants revile and conspire[NOTE:1] against me all day long.
notes: The nature of the acrostic changes here. Each of the three lines in each verse, not just the first, begins with the corresponding letter of the alphabet.

verses.zh: 求 你 觀 看 ， 他 們 坐 下 ， 起 來 ， 都 以 我 為 歌 曲 。
verses.en: Watch them from morning to evening;[NOTE:1] I am the object of their mocking songs.
notes: The nature of the acrostic changes here. Each of the three lines in each verse, not just the first, begins with the corresponding letter of the alphabet.

verses.zh: 耶 和 華 啊 ， 你 要 按 著 他 們 手 所 做 的 向 他 們 施 行 報 應 。
verses.en: ת (Tav)Pay them back[NOTE:1] what they deserve,[NOTE:2] O Lord,according to what they[NOTE:3] have done.[NOTE:4]
notes: The nature of the acrostic changes here. Each of the three lines in each verse, not just the first, begins with the corresponding letter of the alphabet.

The noun שֵׁבֶט (shevet, “rod”) refers to the weapon used for smiting an enemy (Exod 21:20; 2 Sam 23:21; 1 Chr 11:3; Isa 10:15; Mic 4:14 HT [5:1 ET]) and to the instrument of child-discipline (Prov 10:13; 22:15; 29:15). It is used figuratively to describe discipline of the individual (Job 9:34; 21:9; 37:13; 2 Sam 7:14; Ps 89:33) and the nation (Isa 10:5, 24; 14:29; 30:31).

verses.zh: 你 要 使 他 們 心 裡 剛 硬 ， 使 你 的 咒 詛 臨 到 他 們 。
verses.en: Give them a distraught heart;[NOTE:1] may your curse be on them!
notes: The nature of the acrostic changes here. Each of the three lines in each verse, not just the first, begins with the corresponding letter of the alphabet.

verses.zh: 你 要 發 怒 追 趕 他 們 ， 從 耶 和 華 的 天 下 除 滅 他 們 。
verses.en: Pursue them[NOTE:1] in anger and eradicate themfrom under the Lord’s heaven.
notes: The nature of the acrostic changes here. Each of the three lines in each verse, not just the first, begins with the corresponding letter of the alphabet.
